brief_summary: Side-by-side cross-section of a switch stem inside its housing rails. Left panel ('fresh application') shows uneven amber lube blobs clustered unevenly along the rail contact with a bare patch. Right panel ('after repeated actuation') shows the same contact band redistributed into one thin, even amber-highlighted strip with a focal ring marking the smoothed surface.
data_sources: switch-break-in-myth.mdx § 'What's actually moving in there' — 'A factory or hand lube job is rarely a perfectly even film ... Over a few hundred cycles, an uneven application tends to even out: thick spots get pushed thin, thin spots pick up a little of what migrated off the thick ones.'
